            "## 🔧 Plotto Studio v5: Scene Parts & Continuity\n\nI've continued developing the actual application, concentrating on two things: **Cook's partial-conflict notation** and **checking continuity across a constructed story**.\n\n### [Download Plotto Studio v5](sandbox:/mnt/data/plotto-studio-continuity-v5.html)\n\nThis remains a self-contained, offline HTML application containing the extracted Plotto database.\n\n### What's new\n\n| Feature | Status |\n|---|---|\n| All 1,462 numbered conflicts | ✅ Included |\n| A/B/C Masterplot composer | ✅ |\n| Automatic forward/backward plot generation | ✅ |\n| Character names and local substitutions | ✅ Basic support |\n| **Select individual portions of a conflict** | ✅ New |\n| **Preserve selected portions in story codes** | ✅ New |\n| **Detect repeated situations** | ✅ New |\n| **Flag uncertain cross-references** | ✅ New |\n| **Identify missing character assignments** | ✅ Expanded |\n| Complete semantic continuity checking | ⏳ |\n\n### 1. Cook's partial-conflict system\n\nThis is a significant addition.\n\nCook uses asterisks to divide certain conflicts into smaller dramatic units. Previously, our program treated each conflict as essentially indivisible.\n\nNow, when you add a conflict to your story, you can select its complete text or an individual asterisk-delimited portion.\n\nFor example, a two-part situation might contain:\n\n**Part 1:** A character undertakes an action.\n\n**Part 2:** The action creates an unexpected consequence.\n\nThe new selector allows you to use either portion separately.\n\nThis matters because the same situation can now contribute different dramatic functions to different stories.\n\n**Important limitation:** The current implementation recognizes asterisk boundaries but does not yet fully interpret every specialized partial-reference expression in Cook's grammar.\n\n### 2. Better continuity auditing\n\nThe story builder now examines the assembled sequence and reports basic structural warnings.\n\nIt can flag repeated situations, unresolved links, unsupported transformations, and missing character assignments.\n\nIt still cannot reliably determine whether a character's actions, knowledge, or circumstances contradict earlier events.\n\nThat's the next level of continuity checking.\n\n### 3. Story addresses now preserve scene selections\n\nThe new portable format begins with **`PS5.`**\n\nIt preserves the Masterplot combination, ordered situations, chosen variants, selected scene portions, character assignments, and generation parameters.\n\nYou can copy the complete address, store it in a text file, and restore the construction.\n\nEarlier PS1, PS3, and PS4 addresses remain supported.\n\n---\n\n## An architectural improvement I'd make next\n\nWe've now developed several individual capabilities, but they're accumulating inside one increasingly large application.\n\nBefore adding much more, I want to give Plotto Studio a proper **narrative state model**.\n\nThat means tracking not just the characters but what happens to them.\n\nFor example:\n\n| Story event | State change |\n|---|---|\n| A discovers an object | A knows the object exists |\n| A gives the object to B | Possession changes |\n| B conceals the object | Another character may lack information |\n| A discovers the deception | Knowledge changes |\n| B attempts reconciliation | Relationship changes |\n\nThe application could track these operations as an editable ledger.\n\nThis would enable genuinely useful continuity checks without requiring AI to invent explanations.\n\nIt would also support your source-constrained songwriting project: **the dramatic consequences can become structural elements of the musical arrangement.**\n\n### Development files\n\n**[Plotto Studio v5](sandbox:/mnt/data/plotto-studio-continuity-v5.html)**\n\n**[Python build script](sandbox:/mnt/data/build_plotto_v5.py)**\n\nThe JavaScript passed syntax checking. An interactive browser test was attempted, but the test environment lacked the required Chromium executable. Consequently, this is still a development build rather than a fully browser-validated release.\n\n**Next milestone: a character-and-object state ledger, followed by continuity-aware automatic plot generation.** That will move us from arranging connected situations toward constructing stories in which actions have persistent consequences."
